text: DSH Auto Continue（DSH 插件，Web 客户端）：自动恢复意外中断的会话。它在 DSH host 中监听会话事件，通过 agent.followup 发送续跑文本，并在 Web 界面提供设置卡片、会话开关和模式菜单。功能包括按错误类型恢复、重启后扫描中断会话、续跑静默回合、可选的成功回合自主循环，以及识别重复输出或工具调用的循环守卫。适合希望减少手动恢复并管理长任务的 DSH 用户；无需额外 API Key 或第三方服务。

DSH Auto Continue resumes interrupted sessions through the host. The Web UI provides per-session controls. It classifies failures, scans sessions on startup, resumes silent turns, optionally continues completed turns, and interrupts repetitive output or tool calls. No extra API key is needed.
DSH 会话因为网络错误停住后，能不能等一会儿自动发继续？
我想让 DSH 重启后找回最近中断的任务并接着跑。
能为每个对话单独选择关闭、只恢复故障或持续自动续跑吗？
模型只输出了思考，没有回复或调用工具时，怎样让它继续生成？
我希望失败重试之间逐渐拉长等待时间，并能限制连续尝试次数。
有没有办法发现模型一直重复回答或反复调用同一个工具并打断它？
自动续跑前能检查上一步工具是否完成，并提醒不要重复执行吗？
我想在 DSH 输入框旁边暂停某个会话的自动续跑，或临时恢复一次。
Can DSH resume a session automatically after a temporary request error?
I want a per-conversation choice between recovery only and continuing after every completed turn.
How can I spot a model repeating itself and interrupt a loop while the turn is still running?
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「中断恢复」：检测可恢复的错误或输出上限中断，在宽限期后发送续跑文本；错误分类可跳过永久错误。可配置冷却、连续次数和自适应退避。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「启动扫描」：host 启动后检查时间窗内的中断会话，也会扫描尚未载入的持久化会话；符合条件的会话会恢复到 agent 注册表并进入常规恢复流程。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「静默回合恢复」：当观察到模型活动但没有可见回复或工具调用时，可发送专用续跑文本；没有模型活动的空回合不会因此触发。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「自主循环」：默认关闭；开启后，在有可见输出的正常回合结束时等待宽限期，再发送单独配置的循环文本并继续下一轮。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「循环守卫」：监测重复消息、流式段落近似复读、短句空转和相同工具调用结果；命中阈值时取消当前回合并安排带提示文本的续跑。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「会话模式控制」：在输入框旁为当前会话提供开关和模式菜单，可选跟随默认、关闭、仅恢复故障或自主循环；设置保存到 host。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「运行状态面板」：设置卡片展示当日续跑、恢复、失败、跳过、放弃和循环中断统计，也列出近期恢复尝试及暂停的会话。
DSH Auto Continue 的功能「续跑模板」：可分别设置一般错误、输出上限、静默回合、重启中断和自主循环的文本，并插入错误码、消息、工具名、回合数或耗时等上下文。

dsh-auto-continue

Recover interrupted DSH sessions automatically, with an optional loop to continue after successful turns.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：Automatic recovery for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), in the Web UI and desktop app. When a recoverable failure interrupts a session, the plugin sends your configured continuation prompt through DSH. The engine runs **inside the host process**, so it keeps watching while browser tabs are closed; all tabs share that engine. Recovery is enabled by default. Continuing after successful turns is a separate, **opt-in autonomous loop**.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：

**Smart recovery** (all configurable):

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：- **Session modes** — switch auto-continue on or off beside the message input, for that conversation only. The mode menu next to the switch shows the current mode and opens Follow default, Off, Recovery only or Autonomous loop. Choices save on the host, survive restarts and sync across tabs; hiding the control does not change them
- **Error classification** — transient failures (network / timeout / 5xx / 429…) are auto-resumed; permanent ones are **skipped** and notified, because retrying them never helps. A failure counts as permanent when its HTTP status is 401/403 or its code/message matches auth, credential/API-key, balance/quota, unknown-model, or context-length/overflow keywords. Provider-specific exceptions can be opted into with literal custom retryable patterns; turn classification off to resume everything
- **Adaptive backoff** — consecutive failures wait longer each time (cooldown × factor: 20s → 40s → 80s…), capped at the max backoff, instead of hammering a broken upstream
- **English / Chinese localization** — the settings card uses DSH's locale service. Built-in resume / guard / loop text and browser notifications use Chi

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：| Event | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `turn/end` → `error` | Turn failed (model / network / timeout, …) |
| `turn/end` → `interrupted` | Crash-orphaned turn left behind by a host restart (recovered by the startup scan) |
| `turn/end` → `max-tokens` | Output token ceiling reached |
| `turn/end` → `completed` / `no-visible-output` with no visible output | Observed model activity without visible output, or an explicit silent-ending marker |
| `turn/end` → `completed` | Continue a normal completion only when autonomous loop is enabled |

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：**Recovery stops for:** manual Stop, policy rejection (`blocked`), paused sessions, subagent sessions and the consecutive-attempt cap. A new turn or manual user message cancels a queued continuation. Live `interrupted` markers are left to the startup recovery scan. Recoverable failures during cooldown are **deferred**, not discarded. If an interrupted session already has queued turns, the continuation runs first and the existing turns retain their order behind it. The loop guard can separately cancel and restart a running turn that is repeating itself.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · What It Does：Subagent sessions stay under their parent agent's control. The plugin skips them during live recovery and startup scanning, ignores **Resume now** for them, and leaves them out of loop-guard cancellation. Any queued recovery is cancelled when a session is identified as a subagent.

---

dsh-client-auto-continue README · How It Works：The host-side engine subscribes to the session event firehose inside the dsh host process — one engine shared by every browser tab. On an interruption it waits a **grace period** (default 3 s) — if the host starts a new turn by itself (`turn/start`), the auto-continue is cancelled — then sends the configured text through the agent registry (`agent.followup`, the same queue the Send button uses). When that queue already contains turns, the engine promotes only its newly inserted continuation before the host wakes the agent; it does not remove or reorder the queued user turns.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · How It Works：On host boot it also scans the live sessions: a session whose last turn ended with a non-human reason **within the scan window** (default 15 minutes), with no later `turn/start` or user message, gets resumed automatically too (e.g. the host crashed while the browser was closed — the agent-loop resumes the session and the engine picks it up). Persisted sessions the host never reloaded are enumerated from session storage and materialized into the registry first; a journal that stopped mid-turn is completed with an interrupted marker on read, so restart-orphaned turns are recovered the same way.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · How It Works：Storage scanning runs separately from live-session recovery. Each storage read has a five-second timeout, and the scan yields every 16 observations without waiting for the next polling interval. This lets recently interrupted sessions deep in the storage listing be reached within the startup window. Recovery restores the session's preset and recorded model; stopping the plugin cancels pending storage work.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · How It Works：Startup recovery isolates failures per session. If history cannot be read or contains invalid events, that session is skipped for the current startup scan and an error is logged; other sessions can still recover, without losing a recovery slot. Invalid entries are not silently removed, since they could hide a manual stop or a newer turn. Valid empty histories and a registry that is still loading remain retryable within the scan window. Reloading a repaired session as a new session object also makes it eligible for scanning again. See [#58](https://github.com/HsiangNianian/dsh-auto-continue/issues/58).

dsh-client-auto-continue README · How It Works：The browser provides the settings card and the composer switch and mode menu, plus a status bridge that shows notifications (with Resume now / Pause this session 1h buttons, routed back to the host engine) and feeds the card's stats / paused-sessions panels.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Recovery workflow：The diagram summarizes the automatic recovery path, the loop-guard restart path, and the exit to human intervention. Click it to open the full-size version.

[](docs/auto-continue-workflow.en.svg)

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Compatibility：DSH 0.1.0-rc.6 and earlier are unsupported. Automated settings and compatibility checks cover **0.1.7-rc.2**, **0.2.0-rc.1**, **0.2.1-alpha.1** and **0.2.1-rc.2**; startup failure isolation is also checked against **0.2.0-rc.2** and **0.2.1-alpha.1**. Desktop app versions and embedded DSH runtime versions are different; use the runtime version when checking compatibility. For the CLI, run `dsh --version`; see [official DSH releases](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/releases) for available versions.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Compatibility：**Plugins 0.11.9 and 0.12.0 are rejected by DSH 0.2.0-rc.1’s version check.** Upgrade the plugin to 0.12.1 or newer; its existing configuration-form integration works on this runtime. See [#50](https://github.com/HsiangNianian/dsh-auto-continue/issues/50).

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Compatibility：On current DSH, **Settings → Built-in plugins** is a component inventory, not the configuration editor. Use the main **Plugins** page. The screenshots below show plugin **0.14.0** on **DSH 0.2.1-alpha.1**. If you previously installed with a symlink or hand-written loader entry, see [Migrating an older installation](#migrating-an-older-installation).

dsh-client-auto-continue README · From npm (recommended)：Published as [`dsh-client-auto-continue`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-client-auto-continue):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-client-auto-continue@latest
dsh web
```

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Updating an installed plugin：Let active work finish and stop DSH. Run the npm command above again to replace the installed version with `@latest`, then restart DSH and reload the browser. Existing configuration overrides remain in the profile. For a desktop installation, update the plugin from that app’s **Plugins** page and restart the app; updating the CLI’s `web` profile does not update the desktop profile.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Directly from GitHub (no clone needed)：Installs straight from the repository's default branch — built artifacts are committed, so no local clone or build step:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:HsiangNianian/dsh-auto-continue
dsh web
```

> This tracks the `main` branch rather than released tags — great for trying the latest changes, while the npm method above is the stable choice. Switching between install sources is just re-running `dsh plugin --profile web add <other-spec>`; the profile dependency is replaced in place.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · From this repository：Use Node.js 22, the version used by CI.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HsiangNianian/dsh-auto-continue.git
cd dsh-auto-continue
npm ci
npm run build

text: dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：A manual loader entry can start the engine without registering a bundle in the **Plugins** page. Use the profile's package manager to install the bundle; a symlink and `insert` entry alone are no longer the recommended setup.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：1. Let active work finish, then stop `dsh web`. Back up `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/`, plus `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` if it exists. If you set `DSH_HOME`, use that directory instead of `~/.dsh`.
2. Keep your existing auto-continue values. Remove only the manually added `auto-continue` row **inside an `insert` list** (and the list if it becomes empty). The installed bundle supplies that row. A top-level `- id: auto-continue` with `config:` is a configuration override: **keep it**.
3. Install with either the npm or GitHub command above. In the profile's `package.json`, `dsh.profile.bundles` should now include `dsh-client-auto-continue`, alongside the existing DSH bundles. If it already does and the plugin appears in **Plugins**, this part is already complete.
4. On DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2, merge any saved values from the old `settings.yaml` → `auto-continue` section or the removed row's `config` into the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. For example, a custom cooldown becomes:

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：```yaml
   - id: auto-continue
     config:
       cooldownMs: 45000 # example: preserve your own saved value
   ```

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：Merge into an existing override instead of adding another one. Keep unrelated settings intact. DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2 reads this entry config; editing the old `settings.yaml` section will not update the new form.
5. Start `dsh web` again and reload the browser. Open **Plugins → dsh-client-auto-continue**, select the appropriate settings category, and check that your values are present. Save a change and reload to confirm it persists.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：The `include:auto-continue` label in **Built-in plugins** is a normal loader prefix. It does not, by itself, indicate a legacy install or a duplicate engine.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：For hosts that expose both modern profile config and the legacy settings API ([#64](https://github.com/HsiangNianian/dsh-auto-continue/issues/64)), the plugin uses profile config without registering a second settings namespace. It imports the `auto-continue` section of `$DSH_HOME/settings-legacy.yaml` once per profile, including the saved pause and custom prompts. Existing profile values take precedence. The original file and other plugins' sections stay untouched; completion is recorded separately from editable settings so even a whole-config reset stays reset after restarting.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Migrating an older installation：Recovery and the loop guard wait while this import is pending. If the legacy file cannot be read or validated, or the profile cannot be saved, the host logs an import error and keeps both held. Repair the file or profile permissions and restart the host. Hosts that only support the legacy API continue using their existing settings store.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Verify & uninstall：```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A 4 'id: auto-continue'
```

The composed config should contain one `id: auto-continue` entry. In **Plugins → dsh-client-auto-continue**, check that the component is **Running** and that the **General** category shows editable fields. With verbose logging enabled, engine activity appears in the terminal running DSH.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-client-auto-continue   # npm / repo install

dsh-client-auto-continue README · also remove this plugin's config override from cordis.patch.yml, if present：dsh web
```

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Troubleshooting：- **“Skipping profile bundle” / “incompatible with dsh 0.2.0-rc.1”:** update to plugin 0.12.1 or newer in the profile the app actually uses, then restart it. A version exemption is not needed for this fix.
- **Enabled, but no configuration fields:** open the main **Plugins** page, select the package and open **General**. The Built-in plugins status page has no editable fields.
- **`/api/auto-continue-bridge` returns 404:** check the DSH startup log and composed config to confirm the host component loaded. Refreshing the settings card cannot start a missing host component.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：The **Auto-continue** switch beside the input applies only to the current conversation and saves immediately

Turning it off selects Off, and turning it back on selects Follow default
Use the mode menu next to the switch to choose a mode:

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：| Mode | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Follow default | Use **Default session mode** from the plugin settings, initially Recovery only |
| Off | No automatic followups or loop-guard interruptions in this conversation |
| Recovery only | Recover eligible failures and silent turns; leave normal completions alone |
| Autonomous loop | Also continue normally completed turns, using the loop prompt |

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：For example, keep A looping, B recovering failures and C off. Each conversation's choice is saved in the host's profile settings (`sessionModes`), shared across tabs and retained after a host restart. Choosing Follow default explicitly removes that conversation's independent policy, including an inherited override.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：**Enable auto-continue globally** in **General** remains the master control. Turning it off pauses all automatic followups without replacing individual choices; turning it back on restores those choices. Switching a conversation off cancels pending grace, cooldown and loop-guard retries. It leaves any current turn running. Switching Loop to Recovery only cancels pending autonomous followups. Re-enabling does not resurrect cancelled sends.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：The notification's **Pause this session 1h** still temporarily suspends one conversation. **Resume now** requests a single send even while paused or Off, without changing the stored mode. The global loop-guard setting remains independent of global pause, but a conversation set to Off is excluded from the guard too.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：To hide the controls, open **Plugins → dsh-client-auto-continue → General**, turn off **Show auto-continue switch in the composer**, then **Save**. This only changes visibility (`showComposerToggle`, default `true`). Hosts without the composer slot retain the settings card. A failed save surfaces as a DSH toast instead of inline red text, and a host that stays unavailable for three seconds announces itself once without flashing on a normal load. The switch and mode menu stay disabled while the host bridge or writable settings service is unavailable. When the composer row narrows, the same container query used by the native permission picker collapses the label to its icon and the mode menu to its arrow, keeping the switch and menu on one line.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Session modes：For DS-Bot / dsh-pocket layouts that remove the query container, screens up to **640 CSS pixels** use the same icon + switch + arrow layout, with pause/error text below. After updating the plugin, restart DSH and reload the remote page to pick up the new styles.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：On **DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2**, open **Plugins** from the main sidebar, choose **dsh-client-auto-continue**, then select a settings category. This is separate from **Settings → Built-in plugins**, which only lists component status. Older DSH versions use **Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration**.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：Use **General**, **Retry strategy**, **Startup recovery**, **Continue text**, **Safety**, and **Status and logs** to find controls. Switching categories preserves unsaved changes. **Status and logs** contains today's activity, recent recovery attempts and paused sessions.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：**Recent recovery attempts** groups the last 20 recovery prompts across the host by session, showing each session's count in that window, latest cause, time and consecutive count at the last send. It works with browser notifications off. Causes distinguish silent output, output limits, request errors, restart interruptions, loop-guard recovery and manual resume. Normal autonomous continuations are excluded. These are sent prompts, not proof of completion or a model-health score; repeated recovery is a reason to inspect the conversation and consider a handoff. The history contains no message text and resets when the plugin restarts.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：The settings card starts with a compact GitHub invitation row, then the category navigation; its fields, switches and default-mode selector use DSH's native settings primitives. The plugin manager above already shows the localized plugin name, version and enabled state. Edits take effect when you click **Save**.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：With **Browser notifications** enabled, each successful save sends one confirmation from the tab where you saved. Turning notifications off sends a final confirmation if browser permission is already granted; later saves stay quiet. Discarded changes, invalid values, and failed saves do not send success notifications. If the browser blocks notifications, the settings page still confirms the save and explains the permission issue.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2 stores these values in the `auto-continue` entry's config in the active profile patch (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` for the default web profile). **Save** applies changes live without restarting the engine. Omitted fields use the defaults below.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：Startup recovery polls every three seconds for sessions that load late, up to `freshMs` after the engine starts. Each settled session history is inspected once. `scanLimit` limits eligible recoveries per pass, so healthy or permanent-error sessions cannot crowd out interrupted ones. Pausing suspends recovery within the same window; unloading cancels the poller.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：The browser mirrors DSH's active language into the internal `locale` field: `zh` and `zh-*` (case-insensitive) are stored as `zh`; every other or unset locale uses `en`. The host applies the same rule when reading settings, including values such as `ru` written by an older tab, so built-in prompts stay English even if the browser's bounded sync attempts are exhausted. The stored value may remain `ru`; refreshing all tabs allows it to converge to `en`. This requires the updated host plugin to be loaded. Leave localized text fields empty or omit them to follow that language automatically; any non-empty value is treated as your own template and is never rewritten when the language changes:

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：```yaml
- id: auto-continue
  config:
    locale: 'en' # normally managed by the browser
    paused: false

<details>
<summary>Configuration files on older DSH versions</summary>

Older hosts store user settings in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` under the plugin namespace instead of a profile entry:

```yaml
auto-continue:
  cooldownMs: 45000
```

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：When migrating from the legacy settings file to DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2, move these values into the profile entry's `config` as described in [Migrating an older installation](#migrating-an-older-installation).

</details>

**How the card works:**

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：- Edits are **staged** — nothing reaches the disk until you hit **Save**; leaving the page drops unsaved drafts
- If you edit or reset a field while a save is in progress, the newer draft stays in the card. Click **Save** again after the current save finishes to apply it
- An overridden field shows a **Reset to default** button that removes the override and restores the inherited value (normally the built-in default)
- Boolean fields use native switches and are staged until Save. **Reset to default** removes the override and restores the inherited value. **Enable auto-continue globally** is on when recovery is enabled (`paused: false`)
- Invalid drafts (non-numbers, values below the minimum) block the save and mark their category, even when another category is selected
- In a read-only deployment the card shows the stored values but disables editing while keeping category navigation available
- Changes apply immediately after Save and persist in the active profile config (or `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` on older hosts)

| --- | --- | --- |
| Pause auto-continue | `off` | Global pause: no live or scan auto-send fires, queued pending sends are cancelled |

| Continue text (autonomous loop) | `Continue` | Text sent on each autonomous-loop resume (same placeholders) |
| Continue text (harness restart) | `Continue. Th

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：Pausing auto-continue stops automatic follow-ups, but leaves the loop guard active. Disable **Loop guard** too if you want to stop automatic interruptions. Invisible-only text does not count as repeated visible output, and fresh tool calls reset the repeated-message streak; repeated tool calls with identical arguments and results are still checked independently.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：For a provider-specific error that is safe to resume (confirm first that manually sending "continue" recovers), add a narrow, stable fragment rather than disabling classification globally:

```yaml
- id: auto-continue
  config:
    retryableErrorPatterns: |-
      Upstream rejected the request as invalid

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：Patterns are literal substrings, not regular expressions. Blank lines are ignored; any matching line wins before the built-in permanent-error rules. Cooldown and consecutive-attempt limits still apply.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Configuration：`continueText` (and `continueTextMaxTokens`, `continueTextSilent`, `continueTextLoop`, `continueTextInterrupted`) accept the placeholders `{code}`, `{message}`, `{status}`, `{tool}` (last tool call before the failure), `{turn}`, `{errorCount}` (consecutive failures including this one) and `{elapsed}` (time since the failure, e.g. `1m5s`) — e.g. `Continue ({tool}: {code})` becomes `Continue (git push: UPSTREAM)`. `continueTextInterrupted` is sent when the boot scan resumes a session that a harness restart had closed mid-turn; its default explains the restart and asks the model to verify external state before retrying. The guard texts accept `{tool}` and `{result}` (a truncated excerpt of the last tool output). The host engine currently leaves `{sessionTitle}` empty.
dsh-client-auto-continue README · Privacy & permissions：The recovery engine runs inside the DSH host. The browser provides the configuration card, live status and optional notifications:

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Privacy & permissions：- The engine reads session events and history through DSH's services. The browser talks to that host; the plugin adds no third-party service or credential store
- Recovery sends your configured text through `agent.followup`. The loop guard can cancel a looping turn through `agent.cancel` before sending its recovery prompt. Resumed agents continue with the session's existing tools and permissions
- Saving configuration uses DSH's settings API: the active profile patch on DSH 0.1.7 / 0.2, or `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` on older hosts
- Retry counters, cooldown timestamps, timed notification pauses and stats stay in host process memory and reset when the engine restarts. Session mode choices (`sessionModes`) and global `paused` are saved with your other configuration
- Browser notifications are opt-in (`notify` setting). Enabling and saving can request browser permission; denied permission is not requested again. Turning the option off never requests permission.

```bash
npm ci
npm ci --prefix tests/fixtures/dsh-0.1.7

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Development：`npm test` covers recovery, autonomous-loop limits and toggles, child-session exclusion, manual resume during pauses, startup scanning and malformed-session isolation, queue ordering, statistics, localization, settings UI lifecycle and edits made during pending saves. `npm run test:runtime` uses published DSH **0.1.7-rc.2**, **0.2.0-rc.1** and **0.2.1-alpha.1** Settings, Loader and HTTP services. It also runs the actual 0.2 profile compatibility gate and checks client activation when one settings provider is absent. Startup recovery tests inject session read failures into real **0.2.0-rc.2** and **0.2.1-alpha.1** Session/Cordis/HTTP components and verify that healthy sessions still recover. These controlled faults do not imply that normal DSH loading produces malformed logs. The runtime harness controls agent events; it does not send requests to a model provider.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Development：The rc.2 check also loads the published client settings service and verifies card save/reset, per-session composer choices, concurrent saves, disk reloads, locale synchronization and a fresh Host read, using snapshots without the removed `mode` field.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Development：The rc.2 restart test uses real agent, query, and JSONL persistence services: it kills a host mid-turn, starts a fresh host without opening the conversation, and checks one recovery with the recorded model and matching prompt variables. The model adapter is deterministic; no external model requests are made.

dsh-client-auto-continue README · Development：After editing a linked checkout, run `npm run build` to write the updated `lib/` files, then restart DSH and refresh the browser. Hosts with client HMR enabled can reload a rebuilt client bundle automatically.

CI typechecks, rebuilds, runs both test suites, verifies committed `lib/` artifacts and runs [dsh-plugin-check](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-plugin-check). The same checks gate releases. See [screenshot capture notes](docs/screenshots/README.md) when updating the UI documentation.
